thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: p99 latency breach for enterprise customer 'LuminaPayments' on dedicated pool lumina-eu-dedicated (eu-central-1). p95=210ms, p99=2.4s (SLO p99<=1.4s).
jem: picking this up. paging oncall. @pagerduty escalate to oncall please.
pagerduty: paging jem (oncall) — acknowledged.
jem: quick check — any recent config or autoscale activity?
derek: no config pushes in last 30m. I see a pronounced tail from tenant `lumina-batch-importer`. GPU mem oscillation + KV store evictions at the same time window.
nana: (typo) sorry, ana here — looking at traces now. there are many long-running requests (~6-8s) with repeated cache misses and a lot of large-context tokenization costs. seems batch job hitting same hot keys and causing lock contention on per-host KV.
jem: runbook steps: 1) isolate noisy tenant with connection drain/soft-evict; 2) apply model fallback to `gpt-lite-quant` for that tenant; 3) if needed, spin up 1-2 burst nodes. do we have per-tenant circuit-breaker enabled?
nana: we do for some customers but not Lumina. we can flip a soft circuit to enforce 5s request timeout and fail fast. that should reduce tail.
derek: suggested commands: 
```bash
# soft-evict connections
redctl tenant soft-evict --tenant lumina-batch-importer --pool lumina-eu-dedicated --grace 8s --reason "p99 mitigation"

# set fallback route
redctl routes set --tenant lumina-batch-importer --pool lumina-eu-dedicated --model gpt-lite-quant

# enable tenant circuit-breaker
redctl tenant config set --tenant lumina-batch-importer --circuit-breaker timeout=5s,max-inflight=8

# burst scale nodes
redctl pool scale --pool lumina-eu-dedicated --replicas +1 --duration 12m --reason "incident mitigation"
```
jem: executing soft-evict now.
incident-bot: Action executed: tenant soft-evict by jem at 2001000045.
jem: soft-evict complete. connections draining.
nana: applying circuit-breaker and route to lite.
incident-bot: Config change: circuit-breaker and route applied at 2001000060.
derek: initiating burst scale +1. auto-approve is on for this enterprise.
incident-bot: Pool scale approved and applied at 2001000074; replicas +1.
mike-csm: I'm going to send a short note to LuminaPayments support: "We observed a tail-latency spike affecting your dedicated pool. We've isolated the noisy batch tenant, applied a temporary model fallback and timeout policy, and scaled your pool to restore SLOs. We'll investigate root cause and follow up." ok to send with no sensitive details?
mike-csm: sending now.
jem: monitoring — initial impact: tenant p99 down from 3.8s -> 1.1s, pool p99 now ~1.5s. still slightly above target but trending down.
nana: digging into traces: repeated KV eviction pattern where large batch loads flush small-session entries, causing cold misses. also several requests show synchronous blocking while loading external prefetch keys.
derek: can we enable read-through cache warming for that tenant for the next 10 minutes? that should reduce cold miss storms.
nana: yes we have a toggle. enabling read-through warm now.
incident-bot: Config change: read-through-cache-warm enabled for tenant lumina-batch-importer at 2001000105.
jem: after warming, pool p95=200ms p99=1.25s. marginally above SLO.
mike-csm: customer replied: "Thanks — we're pausing the nightly import job immediately and will coordinate a staged retry." good signal.
derek: with their pause plus our mitigations p99 dropped to 1.0s within 90s. SLO restored.
jem: excellent. root-cause suspicion: unsharded batch job producing hot-key stampede + aggressive TTL eviction behavior in tenant workload, amplified by shared KV caching on the dedicated pool.
nana: collecting flamegraphs and KV metrics to attach to the incident. will also snapshot the request traces with sampling.
jem: next steps: 1) keep burst replica for 12m; 2) collect full traces and KV histograms; 3) propose follow-ups: per-tenant prewarm policy, per-tenant temporary sub-pool offer for heavy batch windows, refine per-tenant tail alerts.
mike-csm: setting up post-incident call with Lumina to agree on batch windows and possible isolated sub-pool.
nana: I'll open the postmortem ticket and include remediation owners.
incident-bot: Handoff: oncall-jem -> ana at 2001000180.
jem: handing off to ana for analysis. stepping off.
nana: acknowledged. I'll continue and post updates in this thread.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> SLO restored. ticket created: INC-2026-8259.
mike-csm: posted customer-friendly summary and scheduled follow-up for tomorrow.
nana: RCA draft: cause: tenant batch-import job causing KV thrash and hot-key contention; mitigations: tenant soft-evict, model fallback, circuit-breaker, cache-warm, burst scaling; action items: enable per-tenant prewarm, provide recommended batch window guidance to customers, improve autoscale sensitivity on KV-miss signals.
jem: thanks all. close war room when postmortem ticket is linked and graphs attached.
incident-bot: War room will auto-close in 1h unless new activity.
